So, it is true for every natural no. ' \(a_1\) ' as there is no term of \(a_1\) in mean deviation.

A seven-digit odd number must have an odd digit in the units place.

If the units digit is \(1\),

the remaining digits are \(2,2,2,3,3,5\)

which can be arranged in \(\dfrac{6!}{3!2!}=60\) ways.

If the units digit is \(5\),

the remaining digits are \(1,2,2,2,3,3\),

which can be arranged in \(\dfrac{6!}{3!2!}=60\) ways.

If the units digit is \(3\),

one of the two identical \(3\)'s is used in the units place.

The remaining digits are \(1,2,2,2,3,5\),

which can be arranged in \(\dfrac{6!}{3!}=120\) ways.

Therefore, the required number is \(60+60+120=240\)

Let \(P\left(a_1, b_1\right)\) and \(Q\left(a_2, b_2\right)\) be two distinct points on a circle with center \(C(\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{3})\). Let \(O\) be the origin and \(O C\) be perpendicular to both \(C P\) and \(C Q\). If the area of the triangle \(O C P\) is \(\frac{\sqrt{35}}{2}\), then \(a_1^2+a_2^2+b_1^2+b_2^2\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2023, 30 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The centre is \(C=(\sqrt{2},\sqrt{3})\)

\(\therefore OC=\sqrt{2+3}=\sqrt{5}\)

Both \(CP\) and \(CQ\) are perpendicular to \(OC\).

As \(P\) and \(Q\) are distinct points on the circle with centre \(C\), they are opposite endpoints of a diameter.

Let the radius be \(r\).

The area of right triangle \(OCP\) is

\(\dfrac{1}{2}(OC)(CP)=\dfrac{\sqrt{35}}{2}\)

\(\dfrac{1}{2}(\sqrt{5})r=\dfrac{\sqrt{35}}{2}\)

\(r=\sqrt{7}\)

Write \(P=C+\vec{u}\)

\(Q=C-\vec{u}\)

where \(|\vec{u}|=r\).

Then \(OP^2+OQ^2=|C+\vec{u}|^2+|C-\vec{u}|^2\)

\(OP^2+OQ^2=2|C|^2+2|\vec{u}|^2\)

\(=2(5)+2(7)=24\)

But \(OP^2+OQ^2=a_1^2+b_1^2+a_2^2+b_2^2\)

\(\therefore\) the required value is \(24\).

Let a line \(L\) pass through the point \(P(2,3,1)\) and be parallel to the line \(x+3 y-2 z-2=0=x-y+2 z\). If the distance of \(L\) from the point \((5,3,8)\) is \(\alpha\), then \(3 \alpha^2\) is equal to

 

[JEE Main 2023, 30 Jan (Shift 2)]
questions.explanation:
The given line is the intersection of the planes \(x+3y-2z-2=0\) and \(x-y+2z=0\).

The normal vectors of the planes are \(\vec n_1=(1,3,-2)\) and \(\vec n_2=(1,-1,2)\).

A direction vector of the line is \(\vec d=\vec n_1\times\vec n_2\).

\(\vec d=(4,-4,-4)=4(1,-1,-1)\)

The required line passes through \(P(2,3,1)\), so its direction vector may be taken as \((1,-1,-1)\).

For \(A(5,3,8)\), \(\overrightarrow{PA}=(3,0,7)\).

The square of the perpendicular distance is

\(\alpha^2=\dfrac{\left|\overrightarrow{PA}\times\vec d\right|^2}{|\vec d|^2}\)

\(\overrightarrow{PA}\times\vec d=(3,0,7)\times(1,-1,-1)=(7,10,-3)\)

\(\Rightarrow \alpha^2=\dfrac{7^2+10^2+(-3)^2}{1^2+(-1)^2+(-1)^2}=\dfrac{158}{3}\)

\(\Rightarrow 3\alpha^2=158\)

The required value is \(158\).
